numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For integer inputs (non-inexact/“exact” dtypes), `jax.numpy.isclose` uses equality instead of the usual “close” comparison, producing `False` when NumPy returns `True`. Example: `jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` returns `Array(False, dtype=bool, weak_type=True)`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Match `numpy.isclose`: `np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` is `True` (and JAX should produce `Array(True, dtype=bool)` for the same comparison when inputs are treated as inexact/float).
trigger_conditions: Using `jax.numpy.isclose` with integer arguments ("exact" dtypes) rather than float/inexact dtypes
Example discrepancy occurs when calling `jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` (rtol specified as `0.5`)

input_output_examples.source: ISSUE #19935 (casting one argument to float gives expected result)

oracle_clues: NumPy reference behavior: `np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` returns `True` while `jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` returns `Array(False, dtype=bool, weak_type=True)` (issue #19935).
JAX fix described: promote `isclose` arguments to inexact dtype so that `jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` matches `np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)` (PR body).
Casting to float changes JAX behavior to match expected result: `jnp.isclose(6, 10., rtol=0.5)` returns `Array(True, dtype=bool)`. (issue #19935)

category_specific_evidence: np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5) returns True, but jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5) returns Array(False, dtype=bool, weak_type=True)
Casting to a float first gives the expected result: jnp.isclose(6, 10., rtol=0.5) returns Array(True, dtype=bool)
The issue is attributed to how jax treats integers vs floats: for "exact" dtypes, jax demands equality rather than being "close"
The PR test asserts behavior parity: self.assertEqual(np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5), jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5))
reproduction_risks: Behavior may depend on whether inputs are treated as exact/integer vs inexact/float (the passages indicate the discrepancy occurs for exact dtypes).

Behavior for extended dtypes/key types may differ; the PR discussion notes downstream failures for isclose called on key types and suggests falling back to equality checks when dtypes.issubdtype(dtype, dtypes.extended).
